system_overview: This specification models a buffered random access file, which is a caching layer used to speed up interaction with the filesystem. It corresponds to the BufferedRandomAccessFile class in the TLC model checker's Java source code. The specification covers the core fields and the seek, read, write, flush, and set-length operations. Correctness is established by showing that the buffered implementation refines the behavior of a general random access file abstraction.
actors_and_components: The system has two layers: (1) the buffered random access file, which maintains an in-memory buffer, position tracking, and dirty flag, and (2) the underlying file, which represents the persistent storage with its own content and pointer. A separate abstract specification of a general random access file serves as the refinement target. A common definitions module provides shared constants and helper operators for array manipulation.
state_variables: The system tracks eight pieces of state: (1) a dirty flag indicating whether the buffer has been modified but not yet written to disk, (2) the logical length of the file, (3) the current read/write position (cursor), (4) the buffer's starting offset within the file, (5) the buffer contents (a fixed-size array), (6) the disk position tracking where the underlying file pointer is, (7) the underlying file's content, and (8) the underlying file's pointer position.
initial_state: The dirty flag is false. The file length, current position, buffer start offset, disk position, and file pointer are all zero. The buffer is filled with a special arbitrary symbol. The underlying file content is empty.
actions: The specification defines several actions: (1) Flush buffer: if the buffer is dirty, write its relevant contents to the underlying file at the buffer's starting offset, then clear the dirty flag. (2) Seek: move the cursor to a new position; if the new position is outside the current buffer window and the buffer is clean, load a new buffer window from the underlying file aligned to the buffer size. (3) Set length: resize the file to a new length, adjusting the cursor if it exceeds the new length and updating buffer contents accordingly. (4) Single-byte read: read one byte from the buffer at the current cursor position and advance the cursor. (5) Single-byte write: write one byte to the buffer at the current cursor position, mark dirty, advance cursor, and update length if needed. (6) Bulk read: read multiple bytes from the buffer. (7) Write-at-most: write as many bytes as fit in the current buffer window.
safety_properties: The specification checks five internal invariants: (1) the logical length equals the length of the logical file content and the disk position equals the file pointer, (2) the cursor is within the buffer window (buffer start offset to buffer start offset plus buffer size), (3) buffered content matches the logical file content at the corresponding offsets, (4) non-buffered content matches the raw disk content, and (5) if any buffered byte differs from the disk, the dirty flag must be set. The specification also verifies refinement: the buffered implementation refines the general random access file specification, and each operation refines its abstract counterpart (flush is silent, seek refines abstract seek, set-length refines abstract set-length, reads refine abstract reads, writes refine abstract writes).
liveness_properties: The specification checks that it is always possible to restore the buffer-window invariant: when dirty, a flush is always enabled; flushing clears the dirty flag; when not dirty, seeking to the current position is enabled; and seeking to the current position restores the buffer-window invariant.
model_bounds: The model checking configuration uses a symbol set of two symbols, a maximum file offset of three, and a buffer size of two. A symmetry reduction is applied over the symbol set.
additional_assumptions: The specification uses zero-indexed arrays (unlike standard one-indexed sequences in the language) to match Java conventions and help prevent off-by-one errors. Undefined or uninitialized bytes are represented by a special arbitrary symbol rather than nondeterministic choice, which simplifies definitions and reduces state space. The specification includes the general random access file and common definitions as inner modules.
